title: Amber Dissolution Experiment
description: A chemistry lab workbench where the user must dissolve a mosquito-in-amber specimen by submerging it into a coffee mug filled with a reactive solvent. The user heats the solvent, drops the amber in, adjusts the temperature, and observes the dissolution reaction extracting the preserved mosquito.
prompt: Create a single HTML file using Three.js r170 (via importmap from cdn.jsdelivr.net) that implements an interactive chemistry lab amber dissolution experiment. Load both GLB assets using GLTFLoader: coffeeMug.glb placed on a lab bench surface at center, and MosquitoInAmber.glb placed to the right on the bench. Set up a PerspectiveCamera at position (0, 3, 5) looking at the bench origin. Add ambient light (intensity 0.4), a directional light from above-left simulating a lab ceiling lamp, and a subtle point light inside the mug that changes color during the reaction. Create a flat box geometry as the lab bench surface with a dark gray material. Interaction steps: (1) User clicks a 'Fill Solvent' HTML button which triggers an animation filling the mug with a translucent green liquid (a cylinder geometry with transparent MeshPhysicalMaterial, transmission 0.6, color 0x44ff88, that scales up from y=0 inside the mug). (2) User clicks a 'Heat' button which turns the solvent orange-yellow and adds a subtle particle effect of small rising spheres simulating bubbles, and the point light inside glows warm orange. (3) User drags the MosquitoInAmber model (using raycaster-based drag with pointer events) and drops it into the mug. Detect drop by checking if the amber's world position is within 0.5 units of the mug center horizontally. (4) On successful drop, animate the amber sinking into the solvent with a tween over 1.5 seconds, then gradually scale the amber model down to 0 over 3 seconds while changing the solvent color to deep amber (0xcc8800) to simulate dissolution. (5) After dissolution completes, spawn a small mosquito silhouette (a dark flat plane with mosquito-shaped opacity or just display a congratulatory HTML overlay saying 'Specimen Extracted Successfully') floating above the mug. Add OrbitControls limited to 30-80 degree polar angle. Show a step indicator panel in the top-left corner tracking progress through all steps. Each button should only be enabled at the appropriate step.
